subject: Re: Benchmark methodology & SLO qualification — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@edgefin.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Benchmark methodology & SLO qualification — post-call recap

Hi Samir — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the Performance/SLO qualification scope:

- SLO targets you mentioned: p99 latency <= 250ms for short-completion prompts (~<64 tokens), p95 latency <= 120ms for streaming-first-byte.
- Throughput/scale: steady state 200 QPS with sustained concurrency of ~50 concurrent request contexts; burst capacity to 500 QPS for short windows.
- Streaming: client needs partial-token streaming (token-by-token flush) with end-to-end partial latency <= 50ms after token generation.
- Measurement considerations: you called out real prompt mix, cold-starts, and single-region routing (us-east).

Attached: edgefin-benchmark-promptset-v1.csv (representative prompt distribution we captured in the call).

Next steps we propose:
1) Clarify measurement definitions (p99 vs p95, cold vs warm).
2) Share our benchmark harness README and a baseline configuration we’ll run against the model you shortlisted.
3) Schedule a short kickoff (30m) to lock the test window and model variant.
4) Redwood runs an initial benchmark and shares reproducible results and artifacts (scripts, seed prompts, raw latencies).

Can you confirm those SLOs and whether EdgeFin wants p99 over the full request lifecycle (includes network + service) or just Redwood service-side p99? Also confirm preference for single-region testing (us-east) vs multi-region.

Thanks — I’ve looped in Neha (SE) to help with the harness and reproducibility checklist.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@edgefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: EdgeFin Procurement <procurement@edgefin.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Benchmark methodology & SLO qualification — post-call recap

Thanks Marissa — that recap looks right. A few clarifications from our side:

- For internal SLA review we need p99 over the full client-server lifecycle, but for the bench reporting it's fine to separate network (client-side) and service-side p99 as you suggested. Please produce both metrics if possible.
- Cold starts matter for our expected workload: we have frequent deploys and would like a cold-start profile measured (cold defined as empty KV cache and no warmed kernels for the model).
- Concurrency: 50 concurrent request contexts is accurate. We also want to understand tail latency behavior when concurrency steps from 50 -> 200 during bursts.
- Streaming: token-by-token streaming is required; payloads are typically 32-128 tokens. Some prompts will request structured JSON as output (so please keep generation determinism and tokenization details documented).

I'll attach our internal label mapping for the prompt set (helps map to user journeys).

Can you confirm:
- Which model variant and quantization profile you'll run the initial benchmark on, and whether you will include a fallback variant for capacity/latency comparisons.
- An estimated ETA for the initial benchmark run and when we can review results.

Appreciate it — cc'ing procurement for visibility on timelines.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Director, Product Engineering | EdgeFin
samir.patel@edgefin.com

Attachment: edgefin-prompt-labels-v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@edgefin.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Benchmark methodology & SLO qualification — post-call recap

Hi Samir — great, thanks for the clarifications. Answers below and proposed timeline:

1) Metrics we’ll produce:
   - Service-side p50/p95/p99 per-request latency (ms)
   - End-to-end p50/p95/p99 including client-side network timing (we’ll document how client timing is measured)
   - Throughput (requests/sec) and successful request ratio under target load
   - Cold-start profile: we’ll run explicit cold-start scenarios (fresh process, empty cache) and warm runs; both will be in results.

2) Model variant and quantization:
   - We’ll run the initial baseline on the model variant you shortlisted (please confirm model name in reply). Baseline will use 8-bit quantized profile we recommend for production (documented in the harness README).
   - We will also include a non-quantized (fp16) run for performance comparison if you want — this helps show tradeoffs in latency vs accuracy.

3) Measurement definitions / reproducibility:
   - Harness: redwood-benchmark-harness-README.md (attached) explains deterministic seeding, prompt shuffling, and artifact export (raw latency CSVs, logs, and the exact harness config).
   - We’ll include the exact Docker image tag, seed values, and request phasing script so EdgeFin can reproduce runs locally or in your environment.

4) Proposed timeline:
   - Apr 12: Redwood performs initial benchmark runs (cold + warm + burst profile) and produces draft results.
   - Apr 14: 30m results review with you and engineering to walk through findings and any follow-ups.

Next steps for you: confirm the model variant name you expect us to target and whether you want the fp16 comparison. Also confirm whether we should include multi-region (us-west + eu-west) as part of the initial runs or limit to us-east for first pass.

I’ve attached the harness README and included the drive link with artifacts. Neha — can you prepare the run config and share the exact commands we’ll execute?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
